name: Antoni Malczewski
credit: Portrait by Henryk Piątkowski, c. 1880–1900 · Public domain (Wikimedia Commons)
bio: Antoni Malczewski (1793–1826) was a Polish Romantic poet born in Warsaw. He served as an officer, travelled in Italy and Switzerland (he is recorded among the early climbers of Mont Blanc in 1818) and spent his last years in Warsaw in poor health and straitened means, dying there at thirty-two.

His one major work, the narrative poem Maria (1825), is a tale of love and death on the Ukrainian steppe, and is counted the finest poem of the Polish Ukrainian school of Romanticism. Its dark, sombre tone, its refrains and its use of Byron's example made it a landmark for later Polish poets.
